mainEntity.name: What does a Korea Web3 or AI PR program actually cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seven workstreams. One: Korean tier-1 trade exclusive with BloomingBit, TokenPost, BlockMedia, Coinness or CoinReaders depending on the audience, or a mainstream lead with Yonhap, Chosun Biz, Maeil Business or Hankyung for a non-crypto-native story. Two: Korean re-report wave across the remaining trade and mainstream outlets timed to lift inside the same day as the exclusive. Three: international tier-1 re-report through CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, AI Magazine or TechCrunch 24 hours behind the Korean lift. Four: FSC-aware framing baked into every press copy under the 2026 Digital Asset Basic Act track, the Virtual Asset User Protection Act five-minute reconciliation regime and the won-pegged stablecoin bill cycle. Five: Korean KOL voices on KakaoTalk open chats, Naver Blogs, Telegram and YouTube with FTC-and-FSC-aware briefs. Six: on-ground event leverage at Korea Blockchain Week (Walkerhill, Sep 29 to Oct 1 2026) and Korea Fintech Week. Seven: founder LinkedIn and X-Korea activation timed to the press cycle, plus a Korean-language quote and headshot for the lead.

mainEntity.name: Why does Korean press want the FSC framing inside the first three paragraphs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because Korean press treats the regulator as a participant in the story, not a backdrop. BloomingBit, TokenPost, BlockMedia, Coinness and CoinReaders read every Web3 announcement against the Virtual Asset User Protection Act five-minute reconciliation regime, the 2026 Digital Asset Basic Act track, the won-pegged stablecoin bill cycle, the 20 percent ownership cap on crypto exchanges and the Travel Rule. Press copy that buries the regulator paragraph reads as either uninformed of the Korean retail-protection bar or evasive. Conversely, press copy that opens with the right FSC frame and confirms exchange-listing or partner status signals founder credibility before any product detail. The FSC versus Bank of Korea debate over stablecoin issuance is the single most-watched regulatory storyline in Korea in 2026.

mainEntity.name: How does Korea Blockchain Week change the press calendar for a Web3 founder?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korea Blockchain Week 2026 runs September 29 to October 1, 2026 at Walkerhill Hotels and Resorts in Seoul, with Upbit as the Main Sponsor and FACTBLOCK as the producer. The three-day format starts with a private institutional forum for policymakers, financial institutions and senior industry leaders before the open conference begins. The press cycle starts five weeks out with embargo briefings to BloomingBit, TokenPost and BlockMedia, lifts on the Monday before the event with a Korean tier-1 trade exclusive, runs side-event coverage through the conference and closes with a post-event international re-report on the Friday. KBW press demand outstrips supply by 3 to 4x, which is why the briefings start in mid-August.

mainEntity.name: Which Korean outlets are the right exclusives for an AI startup versus a Web3 startup?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an AI startup with an enterprise customer announcement, Maeil Business or Hankyung for the customer-name framing in Korean mainstream business press. For an AI startup raising a Series A or B, Chosun Biz or Hankyung Business for the funding lead with Yonhap as the wire and TechM as the trade re-report. For a Web3 startup announcing an Upbit, Bithumb or Coinone listing, BloomingBit or TokenPost for the trade lead with Cointelegraph and CoinDesk re-reports 24 hours behind. For a Web3 startup launching a KBW keynote, an embargoed BlockMedia exclusive five days ahead followed by an international tier-1 re-report timed to the keynote. For a KRW-stablecoin or Project Guardian-adjacent institutional partner story, Maeil Business or Yonhap for the institutional-partner-name lead, with Coinness for the crypto-native depth.

mainEntity.name: How does the FSC versus Bank of Korea stablecoin debate change Korean press copy in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: It moves the regulator paragraph from a footnote to the lead. The FSC has indicated support for allowing non-bank tech companies to issue won-pegged stablecoins, while the Bank of Korea has argued only banks with 51 percent ownership should be permitted. The ruling party committed to introducing a bill in early 2026 in line with the manifesto from President Lee Jae-myung, and the bill requires 100 percent reserves in safe assets such as bank deposits or government bonds with full custody by banks. Toss filed 24 KRW stablecoin trademarks including TOSSKRW in June 2025 and confirmed an L1 mainnet build in April 2026. Any KRW-stablecoin, payments or RWA announcement in 2026 reads inside this debate, not next to it. Press copy that names a position vis-a-vis the FSC bill, the BOK objection, the Toss precedent and the Kakao Bank or Kookmin Bank application is treated as informed, and press copy that does not is treated as not.
